title: Crucible Feedback Bundle Index
description: Exactly one feedback/index.json per output directory. The feedback bundle is the product: everything Crucible learned about the generator, arranged so a person improving that generator can act on it. Every file listed here MUST be a pure projection of verdicts.jsonl -- regenerable from the verdict records alone, containing no fact that is not already in them.

projections.description: The emitted projections. At minimum, the scalar-reward projection and the preference projection MUST be present, even when one of them is empty (an empty file with zero rows is a legitimate, informative result; a missing file is not).

format.description: How rows are laid out on disk. jsonl: exactly one row per non-blank line. json: the file MUST be a JSON array whose elements are the rows. csv: the file MUST begin with a single header line naming the row_spec keys, followed by one RFC 4180 record per row.

row_spec.description: The exact keys present on every row of this projection, sorted. A consumer must be able to write a reader from this field alone. Every row of every JSONL projection MUST carry 'record_id' -- the record_id of the verdict record it projects -- so any row can be traced back to its canonical record; 'record_id' MUST therefore appear in every row_spec.

eligibility.description: Which verdict records contributed rows, and which were deliberately excluded. Records with status 'unverifiable' MUST be excluded from every training projection and that exclusion MUST be stated here.

recommendations.description: Evidence-backed, prioritised changes to the generator. Each recommendation MUST cite the aggregate evidence that motivated it; a recommendation with no supporting count is an opinion and does not belong in a machine-generated artifact.

target.description: What should change: the prompt, the decoding parameters, the training data, or the schema the generator is asked to emit.

n_affected.description: The number of DISTINCT verdict records affected, not the number of findings. A code that fires twice on one record counts once.

caveats.description: What this feedback bundle cannot tell you. Required to be non-empty: any verifier built on positive-only reference data has systematic blind spots, and a bundle that does not name its own is overclaiming. Every caveat MUST be a full sentence naming a condition and its consequence; a phrase such as 'incomplete corpus' names neither, which is why a minimum length is enforced here.
